public_payload.normalized_proposition: When the AI bubble ends, many people will ask how it happened and will want a bailout of AI companies.

statement.excerpt: When this ends, so many people will ask how it happened, why nobody stopped it, and try and rationalize it within the systems they know. They’ll crave a bailout, even if they hate the companies, because the destruction of allowing things to wilt and die is so unusual within our society, and it’s scary to imagine them doing so.

from_speaker: so many people will ask how it happened
They’ll crave a bailout, even if they hate the companies
our_interpretation: The antecedent is the collapse of the AI investment boom discussed in the post, centered on hyperscalers and NVIDIA.
Many people means broad public sentiment, rather than isolated comments by investors or executives.
Wanting a bailout does not require a bailout actually to occur.
A decline confined to one country's stocks does not by itself establish that the boom described in the post has ended.
criteria.support_condition: After a documented collapse of the relevant AI boom, representative polling or broad, independently documented public responses show both widespread questions about its causes and substantial demand to rescue affected AI companies.
criteria.contradiction_condition: After that collapse, representative evidence covering the public response shows broad rejection of rescuing affected companies, including among people concerned about the collapse. Silence alone is insufficient.
